claim_verdicts.evidence: ShardedOrders.cs lines 54-61: LatestOnShardAsync runs `SELECT id, customer_id, placed_at FROM orders ORDER BY placed_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT @count` through QueryAsync, which opens `new NpgsqlConnection(shards[shard])` — one shard per call.

Demo (ShardedOrdersDemo.cs 30-37) merges `LatestOnShardAsync(0, count / 2)` and `LatestOnShardAsync(1, count / 2)` and counts ids not in the true newest set; captured output: "with 15 from each shard instead: 5 of the 30 are not among the newest". Logic: shard 1 holds 20 of the true 30, returns 15, so 5 are absent; Merge only sees what it is given.

C# async docs: "You start all the asynchronous tasks at once. You wait on each task only when you need the results. ... You make all the requests immediately, and then apply the `await` expression on all those tasks"; and "You compose tasks by separating the operations into a new method that returns a task. You can choose when to wait on that task. You can start other tasks concurrently."

C# docs: WhenAll "returns a Task object that completes when all the tasks in its argument list are complete." TAP docs: "if any asynchronous operation fails, all the exceptions are consolidated in an AggregateException exception, which is stored in the Task that is returned from the WhenAll method. However, only one of those exceptions is propagated by the `await` keyword."

LINQ docs: SelectMany "Projects sequences of values that are based on a transform function and then flattens them into one sequence."; ThenByDescending "Performs a secondary sort in descending order." Code lines 47-52: `SelectMany(orders => orders).OrderByDescending(order => order.PlacedAt).ThenByDescending(order => order.Id).Take(count)`. shard-schema.sql: `id integer PRIMARY KEY`, rows copied from donhang_perf, so rows with equal PlacedAt get a fixed order.

claim_verdicts.evidence: Follows from claim 11 and the code: `await Task.WhenAll(queries)` (line 42) completes only when every shard task completes, and throws if any faulted, so the method returns no list then. The alternative "list that quietly lacks that shard's orders" is stated as what a version that skips failed shards would return, which is what Merge (lines 47-52) yields over the remaining lists.

Round 2 text: a conditioned design rule ("When such a query runs often, look at the reads. If most of them lack the key ... If most use it and a few frequent ones do not ..."), restating outline item 5; kind opinion, no always/never. "eventually consistent" follows from claim 15: a read model in its own database cannot commit in the same transaction as a shard's order.

PG 17 22.1: "It is not possible to access more than one database per connection." BEGIN: "BEGIN initiates a transaction block, that is, all statements after a BEGIN command will be executed in a single transaction until an explicit COMMIT or ROLLBACK is given." A transaction block lives in one session/connection, hence one database; two shards need two transactions, each committing independently.

After the round-1 split, claim 16 is only the saga sentence: conditioned guidance restating outline item 6 and prereq backend.l3.saga; kind opinion, no product behaviour. The two-phase-commit half moved to claim 17.

PG 17 PREPARE TRANSACTION Notes: "Keep in mind also that the transaction continues to hold whatever locks it held." and "a prepared transaction will normally be committed or rolled back as soon as an external transaction manager has verified that other databases are also prepared to commit." Supports the Connections line "at the cost of locks held while waiting".

Subsequently, the query planner uses these statistics to help determine the most efficient execution plans for queries." Matches s5.
